title: Executable FinMR: Arelle-Based Symbolic Baselines and an Executability Audit for XBRL Mathematical Reasoning

contributions.purpose: Provide a strong symbolic baseline for the FinMR XBRL reasoning benchmark to test whether it measures reasoning or XBRL tooling.
contributions.mechanism: An Arelle-based symbolic baseline that reconstructs executable XBRL packages from benchmark queries (href rewriting, linkbaseRef injection, truncated-XML repair) and computes answers via standards-compliant DQC rule semantics (DQC_0015 sign, DQC_0117 dimensional cross-check, DQC_0126 calculation consistency) with a deterministic judge.
contributions.evaluation: 42.17% accuracy on the full 332-instance set and 71.79% on the executable subset (N=195, 0% structural errors), vs best published LLM Fin-o1-14B at 13.86% (a 28.3pp gap) and gpt-4.1 self-consistency at 8.67%.
contributions.domain: Financial numerical reasoning over XBRL filings (symbolic/neuro-symbolic)
contributions.source_quote: We develop an Arelle-based symbolic baseline for FinMR that achieves 42.17% accuracy on the full benchmark and 71.79% on the executable subset, outperforming all published LLM results by 3-5x.

contributions.purpose: Diagnose why the benchmark is hard by auditing whether its instances are even executable.
contributions.mechanism: An executability audit classifying each instance as executable (Arelle loads a valid DTS) or assigning failure labels; a failure taxonomy over non-executable instances.
contributions.evaluation: Only 58.73% (195/332) of instances are executable; 64.2% of the 137 failures are external taxonomy dependencies (recoverable by bundling; estimated to raise executability to 85.24%), plus malformed XML (13.1%), missing DTS (9.5%), unknown (13.1%).
contributions.source_quote: We conduct an executability audit revealing that only 58.73% of FinMR instances are executable, with external taxonomy dependencies causing 64% of failures--issues recoverable through taxonomy bundling.

contributions.purpose: Argue about what FinMR actually measures.
contributions.mechanism: Contrast symbolic execution with domain-specific tools against neural approaches across the full set and controlled intersection subsets, plus href-rewriting ablation.
contributions.evaluation: On the 29-instance intersection Arelle reaches 89.66% vs SC LLM 14.94% (74.7pp gap); without href rewriting 0% of instances are executable, confirming queries are not self-contained.
contributions.domain: Interpretation of benchmark difficulty (tooling vs reasoning)
contributions.source_quote: We provide evidence that FinMR primarily tests XBRL tooling capabilities rather than mathematical reasoning, as symbolic execution with domain-specific tools dramatically outperforms neural approaches.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These are precisely the operations that symbolic XBRL processors like Arelle are designed to perform.
Unlike these benchmarks that focus on free-form text and tables, FinMR (Wang et al., 2025b) evaluates reasoning over structured XBRL filings with explicit taxonomy semantics.
Our Arelle-based baseline extends this paradigm to XBRL-specific tooling, using a standards-compliant engine rather than general-purpose code execution.
Following the evaluation protocol in Wang et al. (2025b), we implement a deterministic judge that classifies each prediction into four categories.

notes: Reports a partial negative/trade-off internally: the simpler Regex Message-Only baseline slightly beats Arelle overall (44.58% vs 42.17% full; 74.36% vs 71.79% executable) due to DQC_0126 calculation-linkbase traversal issues (Arelle only 52.94% with 47.06% CER on DQC_0126), though Arelle wins on DQC_0015 and DQC_0117.
